[b]2025: The Prince[/b]
Crown Prince Erjk Droes was not a morning person, unlike his vibrant wife Vylla who always rose early and went to bed early. However, due to his duties with the various patronages he held of which were the third most in the entire working royal family, he was forced to rise early. As he trudged across the dew covered lawn of Proen (Fish) Palace towards the waiting helicopter he wondered what the day held. He had to visit a hospital, open a school building, and lay the foundation for some government building in the north of the country, shorter than most of his days, and a relief from the normal hustle and bustle.

Boarding the steps of the helicopter he nodded at the guard who waited diligently to simply shut the stairs and door, a young cadet, probably just having gotten his formal rank. Boarding the helicopter, which smelled faintly of cigarettes, his wife Vylla sat in a seat waiting for him, a small coffee table before her, she had laid a pair of lace gloves upon it, next to it a steaming paper cup of coffee.  

Erjk smiled at his wife, an elegant doe with large amber eyes.

Seating himself he pulled out the newspaper he had stuffed into his jacket back pocket, quickly buckling himself in as the cabin crew made the last minute preparations for take off. The newspaper held no import for Erjk, it was merely a habit he had picked up from his father, who once sat for hours on trips reading the paper with a smoking cigar hanging, smoking softly, from his grizzled snout. 

Things had been slightly tense in the family, primarily due to rumors flying about the palace that suggested an affair that the prince was having with one of the courtiers of his mothers staff, while the prince denied the allegations, it had successfully shoved a wedge between Vylla and Erjk that was noticeable to the public, furthering the whispers.

Its a bit cold this morning, began Vylla, in a muted neutral tone that suggested she had little desire to talk long.

Yes, replied Erjk bluntly, brushing off the attempt at conversation.

I read this morning that your mother wants to open the country, continued Vylla, inclining her head towards her husband, who had buried his nose into the paper, reading an ad for a lawnmower.

 I heard she plans to address the Gøsfodde this week, I think it's a rather intriguing idea, he replied, not putting down the paper, his eyes fixed on an ad for a washer and dryer.

The Trade Quorum is certainly going to support any such move, however, I am sure those within the Defense and Security Quorum have their reservations, replied Vylla.

Well, I support any motion to get this country out into the world, for too long we have lain silent, replied Erjk, finally putting down the paper and casting his eyes upon his wife, who was looking out the window. 

You know, the rumors arent true, he stated gently.

Please Erjk, dont bring that up now, I was having a perfectly good morning, replied Vylla, looking at her husband, her ears flicking slightly with irritation.

Very well, replied Erjk resignedly.

The helicopter lifted off into the skies, heading to the north of the capital city to a small town to the north where the couple was to meet with some school children about their new school that had been named after Vylla.
